title: Go: Arrays and Slices
description: Work with fixed-size arrays and dynamically-sized slices.

steps.title: Fixed Array
steps.description: Declare an array `nums [3]int` with values `{1, 2, 3}` and print it.
hints: Array size is part of the type.

steps.title: Slice Literal
steps.description: Create a slice `colors := []string{"red", "green", "blue"}` and print it.
hints: Unlike arrays, slices don't specify a size: `[]string{...}`

verification.failureMessage: Create and print a slice of three colors.

steps.title: Append to Slice
steps.description: Start with `nums := []int{1, 2, 3}`, append `4` and `5`, then print the slice.
hints: `append` returns a new slice — reassign it.

verification.failureMessage: Start with [1,2,3], append 4 and 5, then print.

steps.title: Slice Operations
steps.description: Create `nums := []int{10, 20, 30, 40, 50}` and print its length, capacity, and the first three elements.
hints: Slice with `nums[:3]` to get the first three.

verification.failureMessage: Print len, cap, and first 3 elements of the slice.

steps.title: Make a Slice
steps.description: Use `make` to create a slice of ints with length 3, set values `[0]=1, [1]=2, [2]=3`, and print it.
hints: `sl := make([]int, 3)` creates a slice of length 3.

verification.failureMessage: Create a slice of length 3 with make, assign values 1,2,3, and print.
